title: Reverse Mortgage in Myrtle Beach: HECM for Purchase Guide
description: Buy a home in Myrtle Beach at 62 or older with a reverse mortgage. How HECM for Purchase works, what you bring, the rules, and SC tax breaks for retirees.
h1: HECM for Purchase: Buying in Myrtle Beach With a Reverse Mortgage
dek: Retiring to the Grand Strand? Buy your next home at 62 or older with no monthly mortgage payment.

faq.q: Can you buy a house with a reverse mortgage?
faq.a: Yes. A HECM for Purchase lets a buyer 62 or older buy a home with one closing. The buyer pays part of the price, the reverse mortgage pays the rest, and no monthly mortgage payment is required. Taxes, insurance and upkeep still have to be paid.

faq.q: How much down payment is needed for a reverse mortgage purchase?
faq.a: It depends mostly on the age of the youngest borrower, plus interest rates and the home's value. The older you are, the more the reverse mortgage covers and the less you bring. A reverse mortgage calculator or a loan officer can give you your number.

faq.q: Can you buy a condo with a reverse mortgage?
faq.a: Yes, if the condo is in an FHA-approved building or the unit gets FHA approval on its own (a single-unit approval). The home must also be finished and ready to live in.

faq.q: How soon do you have to move in?
faq.a: Within 60 days of closing. The home has to be your main home.

faq.q: Does South Carolina have a homestead exemption for seniors?
faq.a: Yes. A homeowner who was 65 and a South Carolina resident for at least a year by December 31 before the tax year gets the first $50,000 of their main home's value exempt from county, city and school property taxes. The deadline to apply with the county auditor is July 16.
